correctness.rationale: The nearest-site Voronoi partition is exact because all sites lie on a common circle. Each cell comprises two congruent OVM right triangles; polar integration around V gives M_n(p) exactly. The derivative identity for cos(t)/sin(t)^(p+1) is checked algebraically. Endpoint expansions distinguish p<1, p=1, p>1, while a uniform sine-versus-linear comparison proves the crossover for bounded lambda. Independently reconstructed nearest-vertex distances and quadrature agree with the formulas for tested values; those finite checks are not substitutes for proof.

originality.rationale: The main contribution is the compact-uniform critical-window law and the three distinct exponent-dependent convergence regimes, not the finite-n triangle integral. Bäsel (2012) and Khalid--Durrani (2012) study different distance laws, while Li--Qiu (2016) supplies a broader finite-triangle moment framework but does not state the n-to-infinity nearest-vertex moment phase transition or moving-p scaling function. Pan (2025) handles one exclusion threshold. No equivalent asymptotic theorem was identified by the specified searches; absolute priority remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: Nearest-vertex distance moment is a natural Voronoi quantization and facility-distance invariant. The theorem identifies a genuine nonuniform limit phenomenon: the vertex-discretization error has different decay exponents above and below p=1, a logarithmic critical point, and an explicit continuous critical-window scaling function uniform on compact lambda sets. It is not just a new numeral or isolated evaluation; it organizes a whole positive-exponent family and explains its boundary-layer mechanism.
